description: The harbour bell, striking the watches by the world's clock: as many strokes as half hours of the four-hour watch have gone, in pairs, eight at its end (Smyth, The Sailor's Word-Book, 1867). A bell's partials stand at 0.5, 1, 1.2, 1.5 and 2 times its prime (hum, prime, tierce, quint, nominal: Perrin, Charnley and de Pont, 1982), each dying away over its decay; the strike is heard from the nominal. A point source: its level falls 6 dB each time the distance doubles from near metres, and it is heard within reach metres. Strokes in a pair stroke seconds apart, pairs pair seconds apart. Frequencies in Hz, times in seconds, levels as gains.
